messages:
maya: Hey team - customer (ACME) reports intermittent 503 on OPTIONS preflight when hitting our hosted API from a Vercel Edge function. They see an opaque response and then 401/403 on the actual request. Happens only when the Edge function forwards the browser request (browser -> vercel edge -> our api).

sam: Thanks. Which SDK and runtime? browser fetch or the edge SDK? Any repro steps? :eyes:

maya: Using our TS SDK (edge build) v0.8.2 in a Vercel Edge route. Repro steps: 1) from page do fetch('/api/proxy') 2) proxy route (edge) calls redwood fetch to https://api.redwood.example/v1/complete 3) browser shows OPTIONS -> 503, response type: opaque. Happens intermittently ~20% of requests.

maya: Minimal edge handler:
```js
export const config = { runtime: 'edge' }
export default async (req) => {
  const res = await fetch('https://api.redwood.example/v1/complete', {
    method: req.method,
    headers: { Authorization: req.headers.get('authorization') || '' },
    body: req.body,
    redirect: 'follow'
  })
  return new Response(await res.text(), { status: res.status, headers: res.headers })
}
```

chen: A few calls out: OPTIONS preflight never includes Authorization and CORS fails if server doesn't handle OPTIONS publicly. 503 on OPTIONS strongly suggests our infra returned an error (rate limit, missing route, or a proxy bug) rather than a browser CORS quirk. Also opaque usually comes from a redirected/cross-origin fetch where mode/credentials prevented access.

li: Two things to check quickly: (1) Are we returning Access-Control-Allow-Headers: Authorization on OPTIONS? (2) Does the edge proxy change the request mode/credentials so the browser treats it as opaque on redirect?

maya: Server logs for one failing sequence (trimmed):
```
[2026-11-05T12:01:02Z] OPTIONS /v1/complete -> 503 upstream:connection-reset code=ECONNRESET
[2026-11-05T12:01:02Z] request_id=abc123 origin=vercel-edge
```

sam: ECONNRESET on OPTIONS from upstream = our runtime dropped connection during preflight. Could be a short-lived capacity spike or bug in our edge ingress that treats OPTIONS differently. I'll repro locally with a Vercel edge-like runner.

chen: Workarounds for customer while we investigate:
- Ensure the proxy route responds to OPTIONS itself (fast path) instead of forwarding to backend. Return 204 with CORS headers to satisfy browser preflight.
- Add a keepalive/health route and avoid routing preflights to slower backends.

maya: Customer tried proxying OPTIONS locally and that stabilized the flow. But they're worried about long-term. They also saw service worker in their app intercepting fetch and returning no-cors responses in some builds — which explains opaque responses when SW responds to preflight/redirects.

li: Good catch. If a service worker or another middleware responds with an opaque response (i.e., responds to the fetch event without passing through), browser will mark main request as opaque and hide headers. Confirm if their frontend registers a SW on the same scope.

maya: Confirmed: they had an outdated SW that handled `fetch` and returned `fetch(event.request)` without forwarding credentials on some code paths. We told them to unregister the SW and redeploy.

sam: Action items: (1) Eng-runtime to investigate upstream ECONNRESET on OPTIONS from vercel-edge origin (cc @eng-runtime). (2) Devex to add a note in our Edge SDK docs about preflight handling and a recommended proxy pattern (return 204 on OPTIONS). (3) Support to share a one-line mitigation snippet for customers.

chen: Suggested mitigation snippet (paste into their edge route):
```js
if (req.method === 'OPTIONS') {
  return new Response(null, {
    status: 204,
    headers: {
      'Access-Control-Allow-Origin': req.headers.get('origin') || '*',
      'Access-Control-Allow-Methods': 'GET,POST,OPTIONS',
      'Access-Control-Allow-Headers': 'Authorization,Content-Type'
    }
  })
}
```

maya: Customer applied that and 503s disappeared. They still want root cause. Sam - can you escalate with a trace for the failing timeframe and note vercel-edge as origin? Ticket: https://support.redwood.example/t/ACME-723 (added logs & HAR).

sam: Yep I'll escalate. If eng-runtime finds a routing bug we'll add a runtime patch. Also adding a short doc blurb in /docs/edge-cors about service-worker pitfalls and proxying preflight.

support-bot: Noted — ticket ACME-723 updated with "mitigation: handle OPTIONS in edge proxy" and labels: "edge-runtime", "cors", "urgent".

li: One last note for CF Workers customers: CF Workers will not send `Authorization` on redirects in some cases and has its own fetch semantics; recommend same pattern (handle OPTIONS at the proxy and avoid forwarding preflight) — adding to docs.

maya: Closing the thread for now — customer confirmed stable for 48h after the workaround. Will follow up if eng-runtime finds a permanent fix. :thumbsup:
